q: Do the paper's enrichment claims for unknown-function genes (C8) and ABC transporters (C9) actually hold when tested properly WITHIN the UTF1-unique gene set using COG/eggNOG functional categories rather than whole-proteome keyword counts?
basis: This replication only partially supported C8/C9 because the keyword proxy counted categories across the entire proteome, not restricted to the 1,967 UTF1-unique genes as the paper does. The paper's specific claim was therefore never directly tested.
next_steps: Extract the 1,967 UTF1-unique gene sequences, run eggNOG-mapper / COG classification on both the unique set and the full proteomes of all 5 strains, then perform hypergeometric enrichment tests of each COG category (especially [G] carbohydrate, ABC-transport-associated categories, and [S] function-unknown) in the unique set vs genomic background. Report enrichment p-values with FDR correction. This directly tests the paper's claim on the correct gene subset.

q: How threshold-robust are the reproduced core (2,718) and unique (1,967) gene counts under variation of the RBH BLASTP identity/coverage cutoffs?
basis: The 99% agreement with the paper's 2,745/1,982 was obtained at a single loose cutoff (pid>=25%, cov>=40%). Orthology counts are known to be sensitive to these thresholds, and we ran no sensitivity sweep.
next_steps: Recompute core and unique counts across a grid of identity cutoffs {20,25,30,40,50}% x coverage {30,40,50,70}%. Also compare RBH against a graph-clustering orthology method (OrthoFinder or Roary-for-genus). Plot core/unique count surfaces vs threshold; report the cutoff region where the paper's numbers are reproduced and whether the 'UTF1 has the largest unique fraction' conclusion is stable across the whole grid.

q: What are the origins and integration history of the 3-6x-enriched mobile elements in UTF1 — are they recent horizontal acquisitions, and do any carry virulence or antibiotic-resistance cargo relevant to fish pathogenesis?
basis: The mobile-element enrichment (C7) was the most strongly reproduced claim (127 vs 20-43 in comparators) but the replication only counted transposase/integrase/IS keywords; it did not characterize the elements, their genomic context, or cargo.
next_steps: Run ISEScan + IslandViewer4 + PHASTEST on the UTF1 chromosome to delineate IS elements, genomic islands, and prophages. For each, check GC-skew / codon-usage deviation (recent-acquisition signal), flanking direct repeats, and cargo gene content (BLAST cargo ORFs against VFDB + ResFinder + CARD). Build a phylogeny of the transposase families vs other Nocardia/Mycobacterium to date acquisitions. Report which mobile elements carry pathogenesis-relevant cargo.

q: Are the mycobacterial-style virulence orthologs identified in UTF1 (Mce, catalase/SOD, siderophore, efflux) functionally active in fish nocardiosis, and are they the same orthologs the paper highlights?
basis: C10 was confirmed as presence-only: we verified the virulence-factor CLASSES exist (Mce=21, catalase/SOD=4, siderophore=3, efflux=11) but did not verify functional relevance or that they are the paper's specific orthologs.
next_steps: (a) Reciprocal-best-hit each UTF1 candidate against the M. tuberculosis H37Rv reference virulence set to confirm true orthology and identify the specific Mce operon(s). (b) Check expression evidence in any available N. seriolae RNA-seq during infection. (c) Propose targeted knockout candidates (e.g. the mce operon, mycobactin siderophore cluster) for a zebrafish or yellowtail infection model to test causal virulence. Report a prioritized functional-validation list.

q: How does the UTF1 reference genome's core/accessory structure hold up when expanded from the 2017 5-genome comparison to the full current set of N. seriolae and Nocardia complete genomes sequenced since?
basis: The paper's comparative genomics used only 4 comparators (all that existed in 2017). Many more Nocardia and N. seriolae genomes have been deposited since, which would sharpen the true N. seriolae-specific vs genus-shared partition and test whether '1,982 unique' is really species-specific or just artifact of a small comparison set.
next_steps: Pull all current complete/chromosome-level N. seriolae genomes plus a broad Nocardia panel (>=20 genomes) from NCBI. Build a proper pan-genome (PPanGGOLiN or Roary) to compute the N. seriolae core, the genus-Nocardia core, and the truly UTF1-strain-specific gene set. Compare against the paper's 1,982 figure and report how many 'unique' genes survive the broader comparison (expected to shrink substantially, as in the BVBRC-35 small-comparison-set concern).
